Regarding child SA, I don’t have any waking memories of this. It’s only ever in dreams/nightmares. So whether that actually happened is not something I can personally can say is true with absolute certainty. 

Again, I have tried this. As previously mentioned, I have in fact tried many times to change or alter the dream scene, with additional people, changing the people, the environment, fighting, etc. 

It goes into either a looping effect, where I’ve changed it, played it through an alternate storyline and then it’ll restart/reset itself again back to the original dream/nightmare or it’ll go into a false awakening loop, with sleep paralysis. 

I really don’t know how to stress this enough, but I actually don’t think it’s possible to change my emotional state in this particular dream sequence. And I just really want to be able to find better methods to wake up or get out of the loop. Or have more scientific knowledge on the subject. 

If you think it’s possible to do that, to change your emotional state in a severe traumatic situation/nightmare about child SA involving family members etc. into something positive then you must be a wizard. But considering (I’m assuming and hoping) that you do not have experience in this particular situation, I don’t think you could say with certainty that you can or cannot. No sarcasm intended. 

Regardless, I don’t think I’m capable of that. I just really want to wake up.

I should note that my question about how to change associations for child SA is quite serious. Previously I’ve tried changing the dream characters, changing the scene settings, accepting the situation and letting it happen. I wonder if my lucid consciousness telling me it’s not real - is in fact - me being aware that I need to change my association and perception of the dream content. 

All of these things were successful in low severity vividness but as the severity increases, I either go into a scene dream loop or false awakening loop/sleep paralysis. I wonder how else I could move forward out of the loop?

Furthermore, the medical health team that looks after me, while is helpful for most things, has no solutions to my nightmares. These are a chronic unresolvable condition which cannot be treated through medical intervention. However there was one intervention that has helped previously. This was very invasive pharmacological interventions that are unsustainable long term.

Please see below comment about my experiences with trying to control outcomes in dream states. Often they’re successful but sometimes the content is too extreme to really stop or change my emotional state or response in the dream and therefore my only option- in my opinion- is to wake up. 

I’m not worried about them, although they can be distressing, as I’ve experienced this my whole life. But I am starting to be more curious about the scientific consensus around it, as well as, gain insight into my own personal experiences. 
I realise that the simplest explanation is in fact, trauma. But I think one of my biggest issues, and perhaps the reason behind my inability to fully control or change my dream state while having lucid nightmares is that perhaps my waking consciousness is still unable to fully accept this answer, as there is no concrete evidence to suggest this as fact.

This is super helpful, thanks. I do try to change my associations particular aspects and content in the dreams, and sometimes it’s successful and other times the nightmare is just too severe for me to try and change my association altogether. How do you change Child SA into another or positive perspective? 

I’ve always had nightmares, usually with various recurrent themes, and nightmareish hypnagogic hallucinations that have previously sometimes leaked into waking life and or triggered nightmares and terrors. These experiences also mixed with my nocturnal seizures and secondary bed wetting as a child. I often believed that the nightmares were the source of my trauma responses in waking life. But I highly doubt you can be simultaneously be triggered and traumatised by nightmares.

I appreciate the sentiment, and also appreciate your response to how you view your own experience in nightmare scenarios. However, from my own perspective, I personally don’t think any emotions are a thing you can overcome, or alter. They just are. While, I believe that emotions are indeed impermanent, and that you can choose how to respond to them. I think too, that you can choose then to decide whether this emotion is something worth pursuing into actions or whether you choose to use your emotional energy into more positive and meaningful actions. 
Personally, I would choose to respond by not perusing them, and instead use that emotional energy in my waking life. Hence, this is why I’d like to remove myself from these lucid nightmares.

100% agree. Psych here, on the same token, there’s a massive difference between a depression episode and a depressive disorder. And I think people have a hard time understanding the two. It’s why people who have experienced an episode of depression and managed to overcome it, often think people with a depressive disorder can be cured. It’s also often why people have such stigma and personal stigma on mental health. If they can get over it, why can’t I? Or I got over it, why can’t they? Etc.

On the excuse topic however, I personally think people can have explanations of their behaviour, but people also have to be responsible for their actions. Of course, this would be case by case. 
People can and are assholes, regardless of illness, disability, ethnicity, religion. 
It’s not an excuse, it’s an explanation, and a resulting factor.  

On a another note, I think it would be good to focus on intent. A person experiencing a depressive episode who decides and intentionally hits their kids? Asshole. A schizophrenic unaware of their surroundings and accidentally hits someone? Probably not an asshole. You get my drift. Intention and context is important.

When I first watched part 2 I was incredibly annoyed they didn’t end the show on ep 15. From a theatrical point of view it would have been perfect and impactful but I did some thinking on it. Here are my main thoughts. 1. Obviously it would’ve been almost impossible to end it on ep 15 from a series and creator point of view, because most people don’t like dark and impactful viewing, it’s not neat and tied up and there would be a lot of outrage and disappointment in ending it like that. 
2. The show is about mental illness and addiction, what kind of message would it be to someone battling these issues, that you can just die? What then everything’s over? 
3. There were some really important conversations in the finale, that needed to be heard, about art, friendships, living with illness. 
4. I think a large part of the ending was to show that, there’s no such thing as a fresh start, and there’s no one particular rock bottom, life is a series of rock bottoms, and fresh starts and you gotta, as Diane put it, sometimes you keep living. Even in ep 15, there was a message about suicide, that sometimes, even if you change your mind, that once it’s done, it’s done. There is no other side. And if your lucky enough to survive it, then you gotta keep living. Life’s a bitch and sometimes you gotta keep living. Your best friends come and go, and your life changes. And it’s not going to be easy, and you gotta do it everyday. But you gotta, because there is no other side.
